channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's E-commerce Tax Revenue Surges Fivefold in 2025
item.description: Tax revenues from e-commerce in Kyrgyzstan have increased fivefold in 2025 compared to 2024, according to the Ministry of Economy and Commerce. Over 30,000 Kyrgyz sellers are registered on e-commerce platforms, with domestic businesses increasingly engaging with international digital marketplaces. The ministry is working to improve the legal framework and create conditions for businesses to access global markets.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Crypto Sector Taxes Dominated by Just 10 Companies
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, 90% of crypto sector taxes from January to October 2026 were generated by only 10 companies, with five companies contributing over 80%. This concentration poses a significant risk, making tax revenues heavily dependent on a few major players. The Association of Virtual Asset Market Participants (AURVA) advocates for creating conditions to help smaller companies grow.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Office Requirement for Meta Platforms Amid Dialogue
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a law requiring online platforms like Meta to open offices in the country. A parliamentary deputy stated that measures would be applied if Meta fails to comply, though he hopes it won't come to that. Dialogue with Meta representatives is ongoing, with the deputy emphasizing that opening local offices is a common global practice.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Attracted $709.9 Million in Foreign Direct Investment in First Half of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan attracted $709.9 million in foreign direct investment from January to June 2026, according to Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. The country has implemented laws to protect investor rights and offers tax and land incentives for national investment projects. Efforts to create favorable conditions for investment are ongoing.

item.title: Ukraine Used Own System, Not Starlink, for Crimea Bridge Attack, Reports The Times
item.description: Ukraine utilized its own system, not Starlink, in the attack on the Crimea bridge, according to The Times. The source described the strike as a "symbolic gesture to show Putin's weakness" ahead of a meeting between leaders of the US, Russia, and China.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Fines for Unauthorized Use of Personal Photos Online
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering new legislation that would impose fines on individuals and organizations for publishing personal photos without consent. The draft law, reviewed in its first reading, also addresses penalties for failing to remove illegal content. These regulations would apply to social media users and online platform owners alike.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Online Course Providers to Show Diplomas, Regulates Anonymous Accounts
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing new regulations for online course providers, requiring them to display diplomas or certificates proving their expertise. Anonymous accounts with over 5,000 followers will also be regulated. The legislation aims to increase transparency in the online services market and protect consumer rights.

item.title: COP31 Climate Talks Criticized as Ineffective While Wars Continue Unabated
item.description: The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) is criticized for focusing on climate issues while ignoring ongoing wars, which undermine climate goals by destroying infrastructure and disrupting systems. The article argues that ending wars should be the primary agenda, as rebuilding efforts are highly polluting and war exacerbates climate change.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Require Online Platforms to Remove Content Upon Request
item.description: Kazakhstan's parliament has approved amendments requiring online platforms to remove content deemed illegal by authorities. The new legislation also introduces administrative liability for platforms that fail to comply with removal orders. Additionally, online platforms will need to register their local representative offices. The changes aim to regulate online content and media activities.

item.title: Former Head of Liquidated Kazatomprom Subsidiary Establishes New Holding Company
item.description: Nurbek Karibzhanov, former CEO of the liquidated Kazatomprom subsidiary, has co-founded a new private company, SNTN Resources Ltd., in Astana. The holding company will manage stakes in various subsidiaries. Karibzhanov, along with partners Anton Manych and Yerzhan Suleimenov, brings diverse business portfolios to the new venture, focusing on mining and geological exploration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Media Law to Require Labeling of Official Government Responses
item.description: Kazakhstan's media law will soon require media outlets to label official responses from government bodies. This measure, included in amendments to laws on online platforms and mass media, aims to help readers distinguish state positions from other information. The Minister of Culture and Information stated the rule is crucial for combating disinformation and clarifying official stances.

item.title: UN Approves $18 Million in Winter Aid for Afghanistan
item.description: The United Nations has allocated $18 million from its Central Emergency Response Fund to assist over 824,000 people in Afghanistan facing worsening humanitarian needs and food insecurity. The funding will support seven projects focused on food security, health, protection, and essential services to mitigate risks during the upcoming winter and lean season.

item.title: EBRD Report: Kyrgyz Banks Strengthened, Governance Weakened
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has raised its assessment of Kyrgyzstan's economic resilience, noting improvements in the banking sector and stock market. However, the bank lowered its assessment of public governance due to declining press freedom and adherence to anti-money laundering standards.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Trade with EAEU Members Approached $6.8 Billion Last Year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's trade with Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states approached $6.8 billion in 2025, according to the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Adylbek Kasymaliev. He stated that trade and economic ties within the EAEU are expanding, with increased exports of agricultural, food, and light industry products.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Needs to Attract Capital Through Digital Markets, Says Expert
item.description: Kyrgyzstan must seek new sources of capital abroad, including international digital markets, stated Asylbek Aitmatov, chairman of the expert council of the Virtual Assets Market Participants Association. He highlighted the country's limited internal capital, estimated at $15-20 billion for 7 million people, and suggested digital markets could overcome geographical limitations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Police Response Time Reduced to 10 Minutes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's police response time to citizen calls has been reduced from one to three hours to just 10 minutes. The head of the cabinet of ministers, Adylbek Kasymaliev, stated this was achieved through equipping officers with body cameras, tablets, and modern digital technologies. The country now has 60 mobile police units and updated its vehicle fleet by 95 percent.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai Approves New Restrictions for Media and Online Platforms
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai has approved a draft law introducing age restrictions for social media registration, prohibiting children under 16 from signing up. Online platform operators will be required to verify users' ages. The law also addresses the protection of children's personal data, with proposals to only share age information.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Ban Social Media Registration for Children Under 16
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai has approved a draft law that will prohibit children under 16 from registering on social media platforms. Online platform operators will be required to verify users' ages. The law aims to protect children's personal data, with proposals suggesting only age information should be shared.

item.title: Tajikistan Temporarily Eliminates Tariffs on Gasoline and Diesel Imports
item.description: The Tajik government has temporarily zeroed out customs duties on petroleum products and gases from countries outside the CIS Free Trade Area until December 31, 2026. This measure primarily affects imports from Iran, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan. The move comes amid reported fuel shortages and aims to stabilize supply.

item.title: Afghanistan's Economy Grows Despite Rising Food Insecurity and Water Crisis: World Bank
item.description: Afghanistan's economy is projected to grow by three percent in 2026, supported by a strong agricultural harvest. However, declining household incomes, rising food prices, and worsening water shortages threaten livelihoods. The World Bank noted that 15.9 million people faced acute food insecurity in September-October 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's January-October Budget Revenue Surpasses Plan by 27.9 Billion Som
item.description: In January-October 2026, Kyrgyzstan's republican budget revenue reached 693.8 billion som, exceeding the plan by 27.9 billion som. This represents a 199.2 billion som increase compared to the same period in 2025. Expenditures were 589.5 billion som, up 189.1 billion som year-on-year. The consolidated budget for 2025 exceeded its plan by 395.3 billion som.

item.title: Driver Arrested in Bishkek After Transporting Police Officer on Car Hood
item.description: A driver in Bishkek has been arrested and charged with hooliganism after continuing to drive with a police officer on his car's hood. The incident occurred at the intersection of Chuy Avenue and Manas Street. The driver, born in 1991, was taken into custody, and his Toyota Corolla was impounded. Authorities are investigating the circumstances.

item.title: Court Orders Arrest of Samruk-Kazyna and KTZ Leaders
item.description: A court has ordered the arrest of the leaders of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ). Further details regarding the charges or the specific individuals arrested were not immediately available. This action signifies a significant development concerning the leadership of these major state-owned entities.

item.title: US Strikes Iranian Military Site in Strait of Hormuz Amid Gulf Tensions
item.description: US warplanes struck an IRGC military installation on Qeshm Island on November 17 in response to attacks on US assets. Iran claimed to have struck a US radar system in Bahrain, a claim the US Central Command denied. Bahrain reported further aerial interceptions, accusing Iran of continued attacks.

item.title: Heads of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy arrested for corruption
item.description: The heads of Samruk-Kazyna, Nurlan Zhakupov, and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, Yeldas Otynschiev, have been arrested by the National Security Committee on corruption charges. A court ordered their detention on November 14th, following their apprehension on November 12th. President Tokayev called the situation a "very serious signal of large-scale corruption."

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes intergovernmental commission to address Caspian Sea level drop
item.description: Kazakhstan has confirmed its commitment to strengthening international cooperation to preserve the Caspian Sea's ecosystem and combat its declining water levels. The Ministry of Ecology expressed concern over accelerating climate change in the region. Kazakhstan supports establishing an intergovernmental commission and advancing a proposed interstate program for Caspian water resource conservation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Police Uncover Fake Trading Scheme, 83 Victims Identified
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have detained members of a criminal group suspected of defrauding dozens of citizens through fake investment schemes. The suspects allegedly used fake social media accounts to lure victims into transferring money to dummy bank cards. The total damages amount to 986.8 million soums, with 83 individuals affected. Criminal charges have been filed, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Rules for Social Media Platforms
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to implement new regulations for social media, including age restrictions for users under 16 and increased platform accountability. The Minister of Culture and Information highlighted the need to combat destructive content and illegal activities online. Platforms will face administrative penalties for non-compliance with content removal orders, and responsibility may extend to users with significant audiences.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores Cooperation with Turkish Companies for Nuclear Power Plant Equipment
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering involving Turkish companies, involved in the Akkuyu nuclear power plant construction, in its own first nuclear station project. The republic aims to localize equipment production within the "Atom-Sanot" industrial zone. Delegations visited Turkish enterprises to discuss potential collaboration and equipment manufacturing for Uzbekistan's future nuclear facilities.

item.title: Taliban Tighten Restrictions in Panjshir, Residents Report Increased Surveillance
item.description: Residents of Panjshir province report increased Taliban restrictions, including heightened pressure, body searches, house inspections, and mobile phone checks. Nighttime movement and access to mountains are banned. The local mosque has been converted into a military post, enabling round-the-clock surveillance. Women reportedly live in fear of harassment and restrictions, often not daring to leave their homes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Continues Operation to Remove Illegal Fishing Nets from Issyk-Kul Lake
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is continuing its operation to clear illegal and old fishing nets from the waters of Issyk-Kul Lake. Divers have removed five old nets totaling 500 meters in length. The ongoing effort aims to combat illegal fishing practices and protect the lake's ecosystem. This initiative is part of broader measures to preserve the environment of the popular tourist destination.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Conducts Mock Voting Across All Polling Stations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission is holding mock voting at all 2,492 polling stations nationwide. The exercise aims to test internet connectivity, communication, heating, and accessibility for citizens with disabilities. This year marks the first time remote voting will be widely available, allowing citizens to vote at any station within Kyrgyzstan or abroad.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Law to Regulate Use of Officials' Images
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering new legislation to clarify when images of officials can be used without consent, citing privacy rights. The proposed law aims to prevent unauthorized use of photos and videos, especially those depicting private life. Images from official meetings may be exempt from consent requirements.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Outlines Legal Priorities Under New Constitution
item.description: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Chairperson Elvira Azimova presented a report on constitutional legality, detailing outcomes of constitutional review and future priorities. The court has received over 18,000 appeals, mostly from citizens, and issued over 500 resolutions. 70% of the court's normative decisions have been implemented at the legislative level.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Banning Social Media Registration for Under-16s
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai has approved draft amendments that would prohibit individuals under 16 from registering on social media platforms. The proposed legislation aims to regulate the internet, protect citizens from harmful content and fraud, and adapt laws to modern media development. Regular messengers will remain accessible.

item.title: World Bank Approves $100 Million Loan for Healthcare Development in Uzbekistan's Samarkand Region
item.description: The World Bank has approved a $100 million concessional loan to modernize the healthcare system in Uzbekistan's Samarkand region. The SHIFO-1 program, running until December 2028, aims to upgrade clinics, train medical staff, and implement digital technologies, improving access for 4.3 million residents.

item.title: Only 70% of Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Decisions Have Been Implemented
item.description: Only 70% of the 91 normative decisions made by Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court have been implemented, according to court chair Elvira Azimova. Legislative work will be conducted on 17 decisions within the Kurultai. Some judicial acts have been revised based on the court's legal positions.

item.title: Dushanbe Enterprises Transitioning to Solar Energy for Independence and Grid Relief
item.description: Dushanbe is implementing solar panels on industrial and commercial sites to advance green energy, ensure energy independence, and reduce strain on the national grid. City administration reports that enterprises like 'Farovon D' market and 'Shirin' confectionery factory are installing significant solar capacities.

item.title: Expert Assesses Risks for Kazakhstan Amidst NVIDIA Leadership Changes
item.description: An expert in corporate security believes that changes in NVIDIA's leadership may not automatically halt previously agreed-upon projects in Kazakhstan, such as developing AI infrastructure and data centers. The expert emphasizes that these initiatives have their own investment structures and depend on multiple partners, not solely NVIDIA.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Restricting Social Media Access for Under-16s
item.description: Kazakhstan is proposing new legislation to protect children from harmful online content. A key measure includes restricting social media registration for individuals under 16, with exceptions for communication apps. The initiative also aims to increase platform accountability and regulate online cinemas.
